title: Jason Calacanis on angel investing, startup intensity, loyalty and capitalism
summary: Jason Calacanis explains how he picks early bets (imagine the world if it works), why a well-built product plus delighted customers matters most, and why venture money is jet fuel not for everyone. He argues startups are an Olympic-level pursuit, that learning new skills is the key edge, and that loyalty and gratitude compound.

principles.text: Evaluate an idea by asking what happens if it works, not what could go wrong.
principles.quote: the way to do really well as an angel investor or just in technology or in life is to not say what could go wrong but to say what could go right

principles.text: Outlandish ideas nobody believes in often produce the biggest returns.
principles.quote: in almost all cases the crazy outlandish ideas that nobody believes in are the ones that have the greatest returns

principles.text: The best startups create a new market rather than just taking share from incumbents.
principles.quote: the best startups induce a market to exist

principles.text: The meta-skill is learning new skills fast; know enough that nobody can snow you when you hire.
principles.quote: the skill you need to refine is the ability to learn new skills

principles.text: Back a well-built product and delighted customers; engagement is the tell.
principles.quote: you can tell the delighted customer by just the amount of time they use it that's called engagement just a fancy word for how much they use it

principles.text: Venture capital is jet fuel; take it only if you want to go big and fast, otherwise grow off revenue.
principles.quote: it's jet fuel you only want to take that money if you really want to build something big and you want to build it fast
